university: Mila – Quebec AI Institute (research institute; host universities are Université de Montréal / DIRO, McGill University, Polytechnique Montréal, and HEC Montréal)

program_meta.program_name: STRUCTURE NOTE (read first): Mila is NOT a degree-granting university and you cannot 'apply to Mila' as a program. Mila is a research institute whose ~140+ affiliated professors hold their actual faculty appointments at one of four host universities: Université de Montréal (UdeM, via the Department of Computer Science and Operations Research / DIRO), McGill University (mainly School of Computer Science or Electrical and Computer Engineering), Polytechnique Montréal (Computer/Software Engineering), or HEC Montréal (business/data science). A prospective MSc student applies to a graduate program AT the host university (e.g. 'MSc in Computer Science, DIRO, Université de Montréal') and, in parallel, submits a Mila 'Supervision Request' asking to be matched with a specific Mila-affiliated professor. The most likely realistic host program for Akshat, given his profile and DIRO's dominant share of Mila core faculty, is the 'Maîtrise en informatique' / MSc in Computer Science (research/thesis track, 'maîtrise avec mémoire'), Département d'informatique et de recherche opérationnelle (DIRO), Université de Montréal, program code 2-175-1-0 (segment 72, Artificial Intelligence, when the research is carried out at Mila). Equivalent research-MSc routes exist at McGill (School of Computer Science) and Polytechnique for professors based there.
program_meta.degree_target: MSc (research/thesis track, 'avec mémoire') as primary target; PhD in Computer Science at DIRO/McGill/Polytechnique is the natural continuation for the same supervisor.

program_meta.deadline_fall_2027: TWO deadlines, both must be met, and they are NOT the same date (a genuine trap). STEP 1 (Mila side): the Mila Supervision Request / matching portal is open ONLY from October 15 to December 1 each year (verbatim from DIRO: 'The portal to fill in the application forms and supervision requests are open ONLY from October 15th to December 1st each year'). STEP 2 (university side): DIRO's own admission page states, VERBATIM, 'For Mila programs (DESS in Machine Learning, Professional MSc in Machine Learning and Research MSc in machine learning), the application procedure is in two steps: the deadline for the first step of the Mila admission process is December 15th for Admission in the Fall' — this conflicts by two weeks with the Oct15-Dec1 window stated on the dedicated 'procedure-mila' page; TREAT DEC 1 AS THE OPERATIVE DEADLINE (the more specific, more recently structured page) and flag the Dec 15 text as possibly stale. CRITICAL, VERBATIM from DIRO: 'IMPORTANT! For all programs, professional (DESS and professional MSc) and research (MSc and PhD), the application for admission must be submitted at the time of applying to Mila (corresponding to step 1), i.e. between October 15th and December 1st.' The general (non-Mila) MSc CS deadline is separately stated as 'Fall before February 1st' — DO NOT rely on this later date if applying with Mila supervision in mind; the effective binding deadline for a Mila-affiliated route is on or before December 1, 2026 for a Fall 2027 start.

program_meta.english_test: CONFIRMED — India is NOT blanket-exempt, and the language situation is more complicated than 'Mila operates in English' suggests. DIRO's own admission conditions for the MSc in Computer Science state (verbatim, condition for regular MSc CS applicants): 'To have a knowledge of the French language that allows one to follow courses in French.' UdeM's central international-student admission pages independently confirm a French-proficiency expectation, advertising an 'Intensive university French program' described as enabling 'future students to achieve the level of French proficiency (B2) required for admission to one of our many study programs,' and UdeM publishes explainer content titled '4 things to know about the French admissions requirement.' HOWEVER: in day-to-day practice at Mila and inside DIRO's AI/ML research groups, seminars, supervision, lab meetings, and almost all publications are conducted in English — the French requirement is a university-level administrative/coursework condition (some required courses may only run in French), not a barrier to doing English-language ML research with an English-speaking supervisor. English-test details (TOEFL/IELTS minimum scores, any India-specific exemption) were NOT found on the pages reviewed this pass — GAP, recheck admission.umontreal.ca's country-specific requirement pages directly (the general country-eligibility tool at admission.umontreal.ca/en/who-are-you/foreign-student/ requires selecting India specifically; not completed this pass).

program_meta.advisor_model: MILA HAS A DISTINCTIVE 'MATCH-BEFORE-ADMIT' CULTURE, CONFIRMED VERBATIM. DIRO's admission page states plainly: 'It is not required to have a research supervisor before submitting your application' for a REGULAR (non-Mila) MSc thesis student — the FESP regulations give you until the end of your first term to find a supervisor. BUT immediately following, DIRO adds a specific and important exception, VERBATIM: 'Attention: if you want to be supervised by a professor from Mila, you must find your supervisor before being accepted into the program "maîtrise avec mémoire", by following the application process described here. Even though it is in theory possible to find a supervisor at Mila after the beginning of your maîtrise, it is in practice extremely rare.' In other words: for the ordinary DIRO MSc, admission-then-find-an-advisor is the norm; for a MILA-AFFILIATED MSc specifically, you must submit a 'Supervision Request' through the Mila website FIRST (during the Oct15-Dec1 window), and a Mila-affiliated professor must, in effect, agree to consider or pre-match with you, before or alongside your formal university application — Mila's own FAQ states 'Mila facilitates the matching of students with potential supervisors through the Mila Supervision Request Form.' The two processes (Mila supervision request, and UdeM/McGill/Polytechnique admission) are explicitly described by Mila's own portal as SEPARATE: 'Please note that the request for supervision at Mila, and university admissions are separate processes that must be completed in [parallel]' (portal.mila.smapply.io, paraphrased from search snippet — verify exact wording live). Practically: applicants use the Mila Supervision Request form to name and rank specific faculty of interest; Mila does some centralized triage/matching; being matched does not itself constitute university admission, and university admission without a Mila match does not grant Mila access — both must succeed.
program_meta.ms_research_access: Yes, but the specific 'research MSc' pathway differs from the professional pathway. DIRO's Master's in Computer Science has two options: 'A thesis option, undertaken primarily in a university setting' (this is the Mila-eligible research route — 'Research degrees in the MSc program 217510 involving segments other than segment 77, such as segment 72 (Artificial Intelligence), if the research is carried out at Mila') and 'A supervised internship option, undertaken primarily in a company setting' (professional MSc, not Mila-research-eligible in the same way, though there is a separate 'Professional Master's in Machine Learning with internship' track Mila also lists as one of its programs). For Akshat's stated goal (student-researcher at Mila), the thesis-option Research MSc (segment 72, AI) supervised by a Mila-affiliated professor is the correct target, admitted via the two-step Mila procedure above.
program_meta.notes: BENGIO FLAG (per user's own framing, confirmed): Yoshua Bengio is core faculty at UdeM/Mila and remains the most famous name in the ecosystem, but his lab is extremely oversubscribed at global scale; he is listed here as aspirational/name-recognition only and should not be treated as a realistic direct MSc supervisor — do not name him as a primary contact target in any application. INDUSTRY-AFFILIATION PATTERN CONFIRMED ACROSS SEVERAL 'CORE' FACULTY: Mila's 'core academic member' designation does not mean the professor is full-time on campus — Ioannis Mitliagkas is simultaneously a part-time Research Scientist at Google DeepMind Montréal; Irina Rish co-founded and serves as CSO of a startup (Nolano.ai) alongside a DOE supercomputing project; Christopher Pal is simultaneously a Distinguished Scientist at ServiceNow Research and only an ADJUNCT (not full) professor at UdeM, with his primary appointment at Polytechnique; Golnoosh Farnadi is concurrently a Visiting Faculty Researcher at Google. This is the same 'named professor, industry day-job' pattern already documented at UC Berkeley (Song Mei/OpenAI) and TU Munich (per prior research in this project) — always check current bandwidth, not just the Mila directory title. HOST-UNIVERSITY ROUTING: a professor's home department matters for which application you must submit — DIRO professors are reached via the UdeM MSc CS application; McGill-based Mila faculty (e.g. Tal Arbel, David Rolnick, Golnoosh Farnadi) require a SEPARATE McGill graduate application (McGill's own SOP/LOR/fee/deadline rules were NOT researched in this pass — GAP, McGill CS or ECE admission requirements need their own verification before treating any McGill-based professor as actionable); Polytechnique-based faculty (e.g. Sarath Chandar, and Chris Pal's primary appointment) require a THIRD, separate Polytechnique Montréal graduate application. GAPS FOR FOLLOW-UP: exact SOP/motivation-letter content required inside the Mila Supervision Request form (portal closed outside Oct15-Dec1, not opened this pass); LOR count for DIRO MSc; application fee in CAD; McGill-side and Polytechnique-side admission requirements (SOP length, fee, deadlines, English test) were not independently verified and should not be assumed identical to DIRO's.
